title: People
goal: Describe what someone is like and what they look like, talk about friends, partners and family, point people out in a room — and share (or resist) a bit of gossip.
intro:
Half of all conversation is about other people: *what's your new colleague like? who's the guy in the glasses? are they still together?* This unit gives you the words for personality, looks and relationships, including the English ones young Odias use (ବୟଫ୍ରେଣ୍ଡ୍, ବ୍ରେକଅପ୍).

The grammar is what lets you talk about people precisely: **relative clauses in full** — *the person whom…, whose…, with whom…* (ଯାହାକୁ, ଯାହାର, ଯାହା ସହିତ) — the handy **participle** shortcut for pointing people out (ଚଷମା ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା ଟୋକା 'the guy wearing glasses'), and how to say someone **looks** or **seems** a certain way (ଦିଶିବା vs ଲାଗିବା).

vocab.note: ସ୍ୱଭାବରେ "by nature". ତା ସ୍ୱଭାବ ଭଲ "he/she's a nice person".
ଭଦ୍ରଲୋକ "gentleman", ଭଦ୍ରମହିଳା "lady".

Lit. "talk-saying". Also simply ବହୁତ କଥା କହେ "talks a lot".
ଚୁପ୍ ରହିବା "to keep quiet"; ଚୁପ୍! "shush!" (rude to adults).
From ଲାଜ "shyness". Of a girl you also hear ଲାଜକୁଳୀ.
Can be praise or a warning, depending on tone.
From ଦୟା "kindness" (as in ଦୟାକରି).
ଜିଦ୍ "stubbornness"; ଜିଦ୍ କରିବା "to dig your heels in".
Colloquially also ଘମଣ୍ଡୀ (ghômôṇḍi).
ସେ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ସୁନ୍ଦର "she's good-looking". Also "(in order) to see".
ଚଷମା ପିନ୍ଧିବା "to wear glasses".
English loan, very common. For anyone good-looking you can also say ସୁନ୍ଦର.
A young woman is ଟୋକୀ (ṭoki). Casual — don't use it to someone's face if they're older.
For pointing someone out: କୋଣରେ ବସିଥିବା ଜଣକ "the one sitting in the corner".
ପ୍ରେମ କରିବା "to be in love (with)". "Love marriage" and "arranged marriage" are usually said in English.
In front of family many people just say ସାଙ୍ଗ "friend".
ବ୍ରେକଅପ୍ ହେବା "to break up".
X-କୁ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ କରିବା "to trust X / believe X".
ଈର୍ଷା କରିବା "to be jealous".
Father-in-law: ଶ୍ୱଶୁର (swôsurô). Daughter-in-law: ବୋହୂ (bohu).
Also used for any friend's wife, as a friendly title. A sister's husband is ଭିଣୋଇ (bhiṇoi).
ଚୁଗୁଲି କରିବା "to gossip, tell tales" (a bit negative). Friendly chit-chat is ଗପ.
After the genitive: ତା ବିଷୟରେ "about him/her", ତୁମ ବିଷୟରେ "about you".
Answered by ତାକୁ / ସେ. Respectful: ଯାହାଙ୍କୁ.
Answered by ତାର / ସେ. Respectful: ଯାହାଙ୍କର.

grammar.title: Relative clauses in full: whom, whose, with whom
grammar.body:
Unit 20 introduced the matched pairs ଯିଏ … ସେ 'who … he/she'. In real conversation you also need *whom*, *whose*, *with whom* — and the relative word simply takes the **same endings as ସେ / ତା-**:

**who** (subject): ଯିଏ … ସେ — plural **ଯେଉଁମାନେ … ସେମାନେ**
**whom / to whom**: **ଯାହାକୁ** … ତାକୁ / ସେ — respectful ଯାହାଙ୍କୁ … ତାଙ୍କୁ
**whose**: **ଯାହାର** … ତାର / ସେ — respectful ଯାହାଙ୍କର … ତାଙ୍କର
**with whom**: **ଯାହା ସହିତ** … ତା ସହିତ / ସେ
**which / the … that** (+ noun): ଯେଉଁ ଝିଅ / ଯେଉଁ ଝିଅକୁ … ସେ
**what(ever)**: ଯାହା … ତାହା

**Word order**: the ଯେ-clause comes **first**, then the main clause, which picks the person up again with a ସେ-word: ଯାହାକୁ ତୁମେ କାଲି ଭେଟିଲ, ସେ ମୋ ସାନ ଭାଇ 'the guy you met yesterday is my younger brother' (lit. whom you met yesterday, he is my younger brother).

The ending on the ଯେ-word depends on its role **inside its own clause** (ତୁମେ ତାକୁ ଭେଟିଲ → ଯାହାକୁ), and the ending on the ସେ-word on its role in the main clause: ଯାହାର ବାଇକ୍ ଅଛି, ସେ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବ 'whoever has a bike will drop everyone'.

**Traps**: (1) Don't put the clause after the noun as in English ('the girl who…'): Odia says ଯେଉଁ ଝିଅଟି ଗୀତ ଗାଉଥିଲା, ସେ… (2) ଯିଏ is never a question word — 'who?' is **କିଏ**, 'whom?' **କାହାକୁ**, 'whose?' **କାହାର**.

grammar.title: Pointing people out: participles -ଉଥିବା, -ଇଥିବା
grammar.body:
In everyday speech people often skip the ଯେ-words and put a **participle** in front of the noun — like English 'the *crying* baby', but it works for whole phrases:

**-ଉଥିବା** — who is / was doing: ମୋ ସହିତ କାମ **କରୁଥିବା** ଝିଅ 'the girl who works with me'
**-ଇଥିବା** — who has done / is in a state: କାଲି **ଆସିଥିବା** ଲୋକ 'the man who came yesterday'; ଚଷମା **ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା** ଟୋକା 'the guy wearing glasses' (lit. having put on glasses)
**ନ -ଇଥିବା** — who hasn't / didn't: ପାର୍ଟିକୁ **ନ ଆସିଥିବା** ଲୋକ 'people who didn't come to the party'
**-ବା** + noun — something to be done: ଦେଖିବା ଜାଗା 'a place to see', ଖାଇବା ଜିନିଷ 'things to eat'

The participle **never changes** for person, number or respect — only the noun after it does: କାମ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକମାନେ 'the people who work'.

To say **'the one…'** use **ଜଣକ** for a person (or -ଟି / -ଟା on the noun): କୋଣରେ ବସିଥିବା ଜଣକ 'the one sitting in the corner'; ନାଲି ଜାମା ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା ଟୋକାଟି 'the guy in the red shirt'. This is exactly how you point people out at a wedding or a party.

**Trap**: wearing clothes uses -ଇଥିବା, not -ଉଥିବା — ଶାଢ଼ୀ ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା 'wearing a saree'; ଶାଢ଼ୀ ପିନ୍ଧୁଥିବା would mean 'who was in the middle of putting on a saree'.

grammar.title: Looks and seems: ଦିଶିବା, ଲାଗିବା, ଦେଖିବାକୁ
grammar.body:
English uses *look* and *seem* loosely; Odia keeps them apart.

**Looks (what you can see)** — **ଦିଶିବା**: ସେ କ୍ଲାନ୍ତ ଦିଶୁଛି 'he looks tired'; ତୁମେ ଆଜି ସୁନ୍ଦର ଦିଶୁଛ 'you look nice today'. Add **ପରି** for 'looks like': ସେ ଛାତ୍ର ପରି ଦିଶୁଛି 'he looks like a student'.

**Seems (your impression)** — **ଲାଗିବା**:
• with **ପରି** after a noun or adjective: ସେ ଭଲ ଲୋକ ପରି ଲାଗୁଛନ୍ତି 'he seems like a nice man'
• with **ବୋଲି** after a whole clause: ସେ ରାଗିଛି ବୋଲି ଲାଗୁଛି 'it seems she's angry'
• with a dative for 'to me': ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଛି … 'I get the feeling …' (unit 14).

**In looks / by nature** — **ଦେଖିବାକୁ** + adjective: ସେ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ହ୍ୟାଣ୍ଡସମ୍ 'he's handsome'; **ସ୍ୱଭାବରେ** + adjective: ସ୍ୱଭାବରେ ସେ ଲାଜକୁଳା 'by nature she's shy'. Together they make a classic sentence: ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଗମ୍ଭୀର, କିନ୍ତୁ ସ୍ୱଭାବରେ ମଜାଳିଆ.

**Just like** — **ଠିକ୍ … ପରି**: ସେ ଠିକ୍ ତା ମା ପରି.

**Agreement**: when a person is the subject, the verb agrees with them: ସେ ଦିଶୁଛି / ସେ ଦିଶୁଛନ୍ତି (respectful) / ତୁମେ ଦିଶୁଛ; with ବୋଲି ଲାଗୁଛି the verb stays ଲାଗୁଛି.

**Trap**: ଦିଶିବା is only about appearance. 'He seems clever' (an impression, not something you see) is ସେ ଚାଲାକ ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି, not ~~ଦିଶୁଛି~~.

examples.en: He looks serious, but by nature he's really funny.

dialogue.title: Who was that guy?
dialogue.setting: Lipi and Riya over cold coffee at a café in Patia, Bhubaneswar, the morning after a friend's birthday party.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ଶୁଣ, କାଲି ପାର୍ଟିରେ ପ୍ରିୟା ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ଯେଉଁ ଟୋକା ଥିଲା, ସେ କିଏ?

lines.en: Listen — who was the guy with Priya at the party last night?

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.en: Who? The tall guy with glasses?

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ହଁ ହଁ, ସେଇ! ଦେଖିବାକୁ ବହୁତ ହ୍ୟାଣ୍ଡସମ୍।

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.native: କାହାକୁ କହିବୁ ନାହିଁ, ହେଲେ… ସେ ପ୍ରିୟାର ନୂଆ ବୟଫ୍ରେଣ୍ଡ୍।

lines.en: Don't tell anyone, but… he's Priya's new boyfriend.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: କ'ଣ! ଆଉ ଯେଉଁ ଟୋକା ସହିତ ସେ ଗତ ବର୍ଷ ପୁରୀ ଯାଇଥିଲା?

lines.speaker: Riya

lines.speaker: Lipi

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.native: ଚିନ୍ତା କର ନାହିଁ। ଯିଏ ମୋତେ ଏ ସବୁ କହିଲା, ସେ ପ୍ରିୟା ନିଜେ!
lines.roman: chinta kôrô nahiṃ. jie mote e sôbu kôhila, se Priya nije!
lines.en: Don't worry. The person who told me all this was Priya herself!

culture: Odia speakers rarely use older people's names: a friend's mother is **ମାଉସୀ**, an older man **ଭାଇନା** or **ମଉସା**, a friend's wife **ଭାଉଜ** — and when talking *about* elders or in-laws, always use the respectful **ସେ … -ନ୍ତି** and **ତାଙ୍କ**, even when complaining about them. Relatives comment freely on looks and weight (ତୁମେ ମୋଟା ହୋଇଗଲଣି! 'you've put on weight!'); it's usually meant affectionately, so laugh it off. Avoid commenting on skin colour yourself — it's a sore subject. Young people talk openly about ବୟଫ୍ରେଣ୍ଡ୍ and ଗର୍ଲଫ୍ରେଣ୍ଡ୍ with friends but often say just **ସାଙ୍ଗ** in front of family, and 'love marriage' vs 'arranged marriage' is still a real topic, usually said in English. Gossip (**ଚୁଗୁଲି**) flows at weddings and family functions; the safe line when you don't want to join in is **ଛାଡ଼, ସେ ତାଙ୍କ କଥା** 'leave it, that's their business'.

tip.title: Describing people
tip.body:
- Adjectives never change: ସେ **ଭଦ୍ର** (he or she), ସେମାନେ **ଭଦ୍ର**.
- No 'is' needed in the present: ସେ ବହୁତ ମଜାଳିଆ 'she's really funny'. For 'was': ଥିଲା / ଥିଲେ.
- Soften with **ଟିକେ** 'a bit' and **ସ୍ୱଭାବରେ** 'by nature': ସ୍ୱଭାବରେ ଟିକେ ଲାଜକୁଳା.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ନୂଆ ସହକର୍ମୀ କେମିତି ଲୋକ?
sentences.roman: tumô nua sôhôkôrmi kemiti lokô?
sentences.en: What's your new colleague like?

sentences.native: ସେ ବହୁତ ଭଦ୍ର, କିନ୍ତୁ ଟିକେ ଗମ୍ଭୀର।
sentences.roman: se bôhutô bhôdrô, kintu ṭike gômbhirô.
sentences.en: He's very polite, but a bit serious.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଭଉଣୀ ବହୁତ କଥାକୁହା, ମୁଁ ଟିକେ ଚୁପ୍।
sentences.roman: mo bhôuṇi bôhutô kôthakuha, muṃ ṭike chup.
sentences.en: My sister's really chatty; I'm a bit quiet.

sentences.native: ସ୍ୱଭାବରେ ସେ ଲାଜକୁଳା, କିନ୍ତୁ ସାଙ୍ଗମାନଙ୍କ ସହିତ ବହୁତ ମଜାଳିଆ।
sentences.roman: swôbhabôre se lajôkuḷa, kintu saṅgômanôṅkô sôhitô bôhutô môjaḷia.
sentences.en: By nature he's shy, but with his friends he's really funny.

sentences.native: ତାଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱଭାବ ବହୁତ ଭଲ।
sentences.roman: taṅkô swôbhabô bôhutô bhôlô.
sentences.en: She's a lovely person. (respectful)

sentences.native: ପାର୍ଟିରେ ସେ ପୂରା ଚୁପ୍ ଥିଲା।
sentences.roman: parṭire se pura chup thila.
sentences.en: He was totally quiet at the party.

sentences.native: ମୋ ବାପା ବାହାରେ ଗମ୍ଭୀର, ଘରେ ବହୁତ ମଜାଳିଆ।
sentences.roman: mo bapa bahare gômbhirô, ghôre bôhutô môjaḷia.
sentences.en: My dad's serious outside, but really funny at home.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ଏତେ ଚୁପ୍ କାହିଁକି? କ'ଣ ହେଲା?
sentences.roman: tume ete chup kahiṃki? kôṇô hela?
sentences.en: Why are you so quiet? What's up?

tip.title: ଯିଏ … ସେ, ଯେଉଁମାନେ … ସେମାନେ
tip.body:
- The ଯେ-clause comes **first**, then the main clause picks it up with a ସେ-word.
- One person: **ଯିଏ** … ସେ; several: **ଯେଉଁମାନେ** … ସେମାନେ.
- The ସେ-word takes the ending the main clause needs: … **ସେମାନଙ୍କୁ** ଭଲ ପାଆନ୍ତି.
- 'Who?' as a question is **କିଏ**, never ଯିଏ.

sentences.native: ଯିଏ ସବୁବେଳେ ଡେରିରେ ଆସେ, ସେ ଆଜି ଆଗରୁ ଆସିଛି!
sentences.roman: jie sôbubeḷe ḍerire ase, se aji agôru asichhi!
sentences.en: The one who's always late has turned up early today!

sentences.native: ଯିଏ କାମ କରେନି, ତାକୁ ଅଳସୁଆ କହନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: jie kamô kôreni, taku ôḷôsua kôhônti.
sentences.en: Someone who doesn't work is called lazy.

sentences.native: ଯେଉଁମାନେ ଅହଂକାରୀ, ସେମାନଙ୍କ ସହିତ ମୁଁ ମିଶେନି।
sentences.roman: jeuṃmane ôhôṅkari, semanôṅkô sôhitô muṃ miseni.
sentences.en: I don't hang out with people who are arrogant.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଭାଇ ବହୁତ ଜିଦି, ଯାହା ଚାହେଁ ତାହା କରେ।
sentences.roman: mo bhai bôhutô jidi, jaha chaheṃ taha kôre.
sentences.en: My brother's really stubborn — he does whatever he wants.

sentences.native: ଯେଉଁମାନେ ଦୟାଳୁ, ସମସ୍ତେ ସେମାନଙ୍କୁ ଭଲ ପାଆନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: jeuṃmane dôyaḷu, sômôste semanôṅku bhôlô paônti.
sentences.en: Everyone loves people who are kind.

sentences.native: ସେ ବହୁତ ଚାଲାକ, ସାବଧାନ ରହ!
sentences.roman: se bôhutô chalakô, sabôdhanô rôhô!
sentences.en: He's really crafty — watch out!

sentences.native: ଯିଏ ପ୍ରଥମେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବ, ସେ ଜାଗା ରଖିବ।
sentences.roman: jie prôthôme pôhôñchibô, se jaga rôkhibô.
sentences.en: Whoever gets there first saves the seats.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଅଳସୁଆ ନୁହେଁ, ଖାଲି ଆଜି ରବିବାର!
sentences.roman: muṃ ôḷôsua nuheṃ, khali aji rôbibarô!
sentences.en: I'm not lazy — it's just that it's Sunday!

tip.title: Whom, whose, with whom
tip.body:
- The ଯେ-word takes the same endings as ସେ: **ଯାହାକୁ** (whom), **ଯାହାର** (whose), **ଯାହା ସହିତ** (with whom).
- Pick the ending for its role *inside its own clause*: ମୁଁ ତାକୁ ପସନ୍ଦ କରେ → **ଯାହାକୁ** ମୁଁ ପସନ୍ଦ କରେ.
- Respectful: ଯାହାଙ୍କୁ, ଯାହାଙ୍କର.

sentences.native: ଯାହାକୁ ମୁଁ ପସନ୍ଦ କରେ, ତାର ଗର୍ଲଫ୍ରେଣ୍ଡ୍ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: jahaku muṃ pôsôndô kôre, tarô gôrlphreṇḍ ôchhi.
sentences.en: The guy I like has a girlfriend.

sentences.native: ଯାହାର ଜନ୍ମଦିନ, ସେ ଆଜି ପାର୍ଟି ଦେବ।
sentences.roman: jaharô jônmôdinô, se aji parṭi debô.
sentences.en: Whoever's birthday it is throws the party today.

sentences.native: ସେ ଯେଉଁ ଝିଅକୁ ପ୍ରେମ କରେ, ସେ କଟକର।
sentences.roman: se jeuṃ jhiôku premô kôre, se Kôṭôkôrô.
sentences.en: The girl he loves is from Cuttack.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ବୟଫ୍ରେଣ୍ଡ୍ କ'ଣ କାମ କରେ?
sentences.roman: tumô bôyphreṇḍ kôṇô kamô kôre?
sentences.en: What does your boyfriend do?

sentences.native: ଯାହା ସହିତ ମୁଁ କଲେଜରେ ପଢ଼ୁଥିଲି, ସେ ଏବେ ମୋ ଗର୍ଲଫ୍ରେଣ୍ଡ୍।
sentences.roman: jaha sôhitô muṃ kôlejôre pôṛhuthili, se ebe mo gôrlphreṇḍ.
sentences.en: The girl I studied with at college is now my girlfriend.

sentences.native: ସେମାନେ ଦୁହେଁ ଗତ ମାସରୁ ଏକାଠି ଅଛନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: semane duheṃ gôtô masôru ekaṭhi ôchhônti.
sentences.en: The two of them have been together since last month.

sentences.native: ଯାହା ସହିତ ତୁମେ ଫୋନରେ କଥା ହେଉଥିଲ, ସେ କିଏ?
sentences.roman: jaha sôhitô tume phonôre kôtha heuthilô, se kie?
sentences.en: Who was that you were talking to on the phone?

sentences.native: ବ୍ରେକଅପ୍ ପରେ ସେ ବହୁତ ଦୁଃଖରେ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: brekôp pôre se bôhutô dukkhôre ôchhi.
sentences.en: Since the break-up he's been really down.

sentences.native: ଯାହାର ଗର୍ଲଫ୍ରେଣ୍ଡ୍ ନାହିଁ, ସେ ଆମ ସହିତ ସିନେମା ଯିବ!
sentences.roman: jaharô gôrlphreṇḍ nahiṃ, se amô sôhitô sinema jibô!
sentences.en: Anyone without a girlfriend is coming to the movies with us!

lessons.title: Looks and first impressions

tip.title: Looks vs seems
tip.body:
- **ଦିଶିବା** = looks (what you see): ସେ କ୍ଲାନ୍ତ **ଦିଶୁଛି**.
- **ଲାଗିବା** = seems (your impression): ଭଲ ଲୋକ **ପରି ଲାଗୁଛନ୍ତି**; after a whole clause use **ବୋଲି**: ସେ ରାଗିଛି ବୋଲି ଲାଗୁଛି.
- **ଦେଖିବାକୁ** + adjective = 'in looks': ଦେଖିବାକୁ ସୁନ୍ଦର.

new: ସେ ତୁମକୁ ପସନ୍ଦ କରେ ବୋଲି ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଛି।

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ଆଜି ବହୁତ ଖୁସି ଦିଶୁଛ, କ'ଣ ହେଲା?
sentences.roman: tume aji bôhutô khusi disuchhô, kôṇô hela?
sentences.en: You look really happy today — what's going on?

sentences.native: ସେ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ହ୍ୟାଣ୍ଡସମ୍, କିନ୍ତୁ ସ୍ୱଭାବ ଭଲ ନୁହେଁ।
sentences.roman: se dekhibaku hyaṇḍsôm, kintu swôbhabô bhôlô nuheṃ.
sentences.en: He's handsome, but he's not a nice person.

sentences.native: ଚଷମାରେ ତୁମେ ଶିକ୍ଷକ ପରି ଦିଶୁଛ!
sentences.roman: chôsômare tume sikhyôkô pôri disuchhô!
sentences.en: With those glasses you look like a teacher!

sentences.native: ତା ଚେହେରା ଠିକ୍ ତା ମା ପରି।
sentences.roman: ta chehera ṭhik ta ma pôri.
sentences.en: Her face is just like her mum's.

sentences.native: ସେ ଟିକେ ଟେନସନରେ ଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି।
sentences.roman: se ṭike ṭensônre thiba pôri laguchhi.
sentences.en: She seems a bit stressed.

sentences.native: ତାଙ୍କ ବାପା ବହୁତ ଗମ୍ଭୀର ଲୋକ ପରି ଲାଗୁଛନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: taṅkô bapa bôhutô gômbhirô lokô pôri laguchhônti.
sentences.en: Her dad seems like a very serious man.

sentences.native: ସେ ତୁମ ଉପରେ ରାଗିଛି ବୋଲି ଲାଗୁଛି।
sentences.roman: se tumô upôre ragichhi boli laguchhi.
sentences.en: It looks like she's angry with you.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ଭାଇ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ତୁମଠାରୁ ବଡ଼ ଲାଗୁଛି।
sentences.roman: tumô bhai dekhibaku tumôṭharu bôṛô laguchhi.
sentences.en: Your brother looks older than you.

tip.title: The one who…: -ଥିବା
tip.body:
- Put a participle before the noun: ମୋ ସହିତ କାମ **କରୁଥିବା** ଝିଅ 'the girl who works with me'.
- **-ଉଥିବା** = who is doing; **-ଇଥିବା** = who has done / is wearing: ଶାଢ଼ୀ **ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା** ମହିଳା.
- It never changes; 'the one…' = **ଜଣକ**: ସୋଫାରେ ଶୋଇଥିବା ଜଣକ.

sentences.native: ନେଳି ଶାଢ଼ୀ ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା ମହିଳା ଜଣକ ମୋ ଶାଶୁ।
sentences.roman: neḷi saṛhi pindhithiba môhiḷa jôṇôkô mo sasu.
sentences.en: The lady in the blue saree is my mother-in-law.

sentences.native: ରୋଷେଇ ଘରେ ରାନ୍ଧୁଥିବା ଜଣକ ମୋ ଭାଉଜ।
sentences.roman: rosei ghôre randhuthiba jôṇôkô mo bhaujô.
sentences.en: The one cooking in the kitchen is my sister-in-law.

sentences.native: ଶାଶୁ ଆଉ ଭାଉଜଙ୍କ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ଭଲ ନୁହେଁ।
sentences.roman: sasu au bhaujôṅkô sômpôrkô bhôlô nuheṃ.
sentences.en: My mother-in-law and my sister-in-law don't get on well.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ସହିତ ପଢ଼ୁଥିବା ସେଇ ଟୋକା କିଏ?
sentences.roman: tumô sôhitô pôṛhuthiba sei ṭoka kie?
sentences.en: Who's that guy who studies with you?

sentences.native: ସୋଫାରେ ଶୋଇଥିବା ଜଣକ ମୋ ମାମୁଁ।
sentences.roman: sophare soithiba jôṇôkô mo mamuṃ.
sentences.en: The one asleep on the sofa is my uncle.

sentences.native: ଭାଉଜଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ବସିଥିବା ପିଲାଟି ତାଙ୍କ ପୁଅ।
sentences.roman: bhaujôṅkô pakhôre bôsithiba pilaṭi taṅkô puô.
sentences.en: The kid sitting next to my sister-in-law is her son.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଶାଶୁ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଗମ୍ଭୀର, କିନ୍ତୁ ବହୁତ ଦୟାଳୁ।
sentences.roman: mo sasu dekhibaku gômbhirô, kintu bôhutô dôyaḷu.
sentences.en: My mother-in-law looks stern, but she is very kind.

sentences.native: ବେଙ୍ଗାଲୁରୁରେ କାମ କରୁଥିବା ମୋ ଭାଇ ଆସନ୍ତା ମାସରେ ଘରକୁ ଆସିବ।
sentences.roman: Beṅgalurure kamô kôruthiba mo bhai asônta masôre ghôrôku asibô.
sentences.en: My brother, who works in Bengaluru, is coming home next month.

tip.title: Passing on what you heard
tip.body:
- Rumours: clause + **ବୋଲି ଶୁଣିଲି** 'I heard that…'.
- **ସମସ୍ତେ କହୁଛନ୍ତି** 'everyone's saying…'.
- **କାହାକୁ କହିବ ନାହିଁ** 'don't tell anyone' (ତୁ: କହିବୁ ନାହିଁ).
- **ଚୁଗୁଲି** is gossip with a slightly bad smell; friendly chat is **ଗପ**.

sentences.native: ସେ ଚାକିରି ଛାଡ଼ିଦେଲା ବୋଲି ଶୁଣିଲି।
sentences.roman: se chakiri chhaṛidela boli suṇili.
sentences.en: I heard he quit his job.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ଏ କଥା କାହାଠାରୁ ଶୁଣିଲ?
sentences.roman: tume e kôtha kahaṭharu suṇilô?
sentences.en: Who did you hear this from?

sentences.native: ଅଫିସରେ ସମସ୍ତେ ତା ବିଷୟରେ ଚୁଗୁଲି କରୁଛନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: ôphisre sômôste ta bisôyôre chuguli kôruchhônti.
sentences.en: Everyone at the office is gossiping about her.

sentences.native: ସେ ମୋ ନୂଆ ଚାକିରିକୁ ଦେଖି ଈର୍ଷା କରୁଛି।
sentences.roman: se mo nua chakiriku dekhi irsa kôruchhi.
sentences.en: She's jealous of my new job.

sentences.native: ତାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ କର ନାହିଁ, ସେ ସବୁ କଥା ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ କହିଦିଏ।
sentences.roman: taku biswasô kôrô nahiṃ, se sôbu kôtha sômôstôṅku kôhidie.
sentences.en: Don't trust him — he tells everyone everything.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ତାକୁ କଲେଜରୁ ଚିହ୍ନେ।
sentences.roman: muṃ taku kôlejôru chinhe.
sentences.en: I know him from college.

sentences.native: ଚୁଗୁଲି ଛାଡ଼, ନିଜ କଥା କୁହ!
sentences.roman: chuguli chhaṛô, nijô kôtha kuhô!
sentences.en: Enough gossip — tell me your news!

sentences.native: ସେମାନେ ପୁଣି ଏକାଠି ହୋଇଗଲେ ବୋଲି ସମସ୍ତେ କହୁଛନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: semane puṇi ekaṭhi hoigôle boli sômôste kôhuchhônti.
sentences.en: Everyone's saying they've got back together.
